A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ShifCon research work, with readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.7. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–23 are identical; differences are confined to first-page author/affiliation text and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual benchmark evaluations in Tables 1–2, ablations in Section 3.3, and additional analyses and per-language results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original benchmark results, ablations, and appendix analyses. These retained empirical outcomes qualify as original results.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same shift-toward/backward projections, subspace-based layer selection, and combined MSFT/MCL objective. Appendix A.4 retains the same two-stage training and language-vector updates.

E1.justification: Both versions use MGSM8KInstruct and Bactrian-X for training and evaluate MGSM, FLORES, XCOPA, XNLI, and XStoryCloze. The language selections in Table 5 are identical.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same English-only fine-tuned models, MSFT, and AFP baselines. Comparator membership is unchanged in both the aggregate and per-language result tables.

E3.justification: Both retain zero-shot MGSM evaluation, four-shot evaluation for the other benchmarks, and the same metrics, prompt templates, model sizes, and training settings in Section 3.1 and Appendices A.3–A.4.

E4.justification: The module ablations, language-consistency tests, layer-selection analyses, and representation visualizations are identical. Appendix comparisons of training stages and pooling methods are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 states in both versions that each experiment uses three random seeds and reports their average. Run-count disclosures and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged, including the appendix tables and plots. For example, Table 1 retains Llama-2 7B ShifCon MGSM scores of 48.2 and 35.1 for high- and low-resource languages, respectively.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the subspace-distance definition and SVD reasoning in Appendix A.2, and the language-vector estimation derivation in Appendix A.4 are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about improving non-dominant languages through shift projection and contrastive alignment, identifying suitable layers, and generalizing across model families and scales.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning information aggregation, alignment, and language consistency are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitations concerning parallel-data dependence and evaluation of generative models no larger than 7.5B parameters.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 retains identical hardware, hyperparameters, optimization, decoding, and language-vector implementation details. The code-availability statement and embedded link targets are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4, citations throughout the paper, and the reference list are identical. Removing an author from the title block does not alter the cited works or research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 removes Feng Yao and the University of California, San Diego affiliation, renumbers Renliang Sun's affiliation, and adds a comma after Sizhe Wang. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; the scientific prose and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–11, Tables 1–18, captions, and placements are unchanged. The shortened author and affiliation lines retain the same first-page header structure, and all subsequent pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 only updates the author/affiliation block, minor punctuation, and version stamp. The scientific exposition, empirical evidence, mathematical material, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
